title.value: Facilitating Asynchronous Participatory Design of Open Source Software: Bringing End Users into the Loop
title.justification: The title exactly matches the content of the research paper and is explicitly mentioned as the title in the provided text.
title.quote: Facilitating Asynchronous Participatory Design of Open Source Software: Bringing End Users into the Loop

analysis.description: The paper explores the challenges of incorporating end-user usability concerns in open source software (OSS) projects through participatory design. It introduces design guidelines, two personas representing OSS designers and end-users, and a low-fidelity prototype tool to involve end users in OSS design.

type.justification: The paper presents design guidelines, user studies, and a prototype tool, which indicates it is based on empirical research and observations.
type.quote: Our design decisions were originally informed by related work on challenges of addressing OSS usability from the developers’ perspective and later iterated through preliminary user studies with both OSS designers and end users.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on participatory design and usability concerns in software, which falls under Human-Computer Interaction.
name.quote: CCS CONCEPTS • Human-centered computing → Participatory design.

name.justification: The paper focuses significantly on the involvement and collaboration of stakeholders, especially end users, in the design process of OSS.
name.quote: Participatory design, where multiple stakeholders collaborate on iterating the design, can be an efficient way to address the usability concerns for OSS projects.

name.justification: The study investigates how to better integrate usability concerns into OSS projects, making it a key subfield of the research.
name.quote: Usability refers to the attributes which determine the ease, error-prevention, efficiency, and pleasantness for an end user when interacting with a software.
